summary: Only one no-fee, removable-battery, home-charged scooter was verified: ZAU ES-1000, listed at NT$58,000 on PChome (struck-through 62,000). It is a 1.29 kWh, 9 kg battery you can carry upstairs, charges from a normal socket in 4.5-5.5 h, tops out at 53 km/h and is rated 60 km at a steady 30 km/h, so real range in traffic will be lower. Battery warranty is 3 years (vehicle 2); service is limited to about 42 outlets, 8 in Keelung. Home electricity is roughly NT$0.05-0.12/km by estimate against about NT$0.55-0.93 for petrol. Subsidy class and an official km/kWh figure were not found. Ionex plug-in models still need a plan from NT$318 a month, so they are not no-fee. Fixed charging in shared areas of an apartment needs committee consent; Kaohsiung's community subsidy closed 2026-08-31. Honest bottom line: no no-fee model matches a 125cc on speed and range.

findings.subject: ZAU ES-1000 home electricity cost per km (derived)
findings.verifierNote: Arithmetic checks out from the verified spec (1.29 kWh/60 km = 0.0215 kWh/km best case). Charger loss and real-traffic penalty are assumptions; no official km/kWh label figure found. Tariff 1.68-3.03 NTD/kWh not re-verified here. Note ZAU's own range is a 30 km/h constant-speed test, so at 40-50 km/h expect a lot less range.

findings.subject: Ionex plug-in under rental plan
findings.verifierNote: All figures confirmed on the live page: 318 plan (NT$250 credit, pure charging about 6.8 kWh / 212 km), 518 plan (17.6 kWh / 552 km), overage NT$52/kWh effective 2026-09-01, NT$15/kWh charging credit, plans effective 2026-08-17. The derived example is arithmetic-consistent: 250/(52-15) = 6.76 kWh, and 12 kWh gives 318+(12-6.8)*37 = about NT$510/month. Addition: the single-battery plan list explicitly includes COZY, so even the micro Cozy appears to be on a plan; the first sweep's claim that the Mint/Cozy micro models are no-fee is not supported by this page (only a legacy 終身免基本費 plan exists for existing owners).

findings.subject: Cheapest home-charged substitute
findings.verifierNote: Verdict stands with caveats: ES-1000 (NT$58,000, 53 km/h, 60 km at a constant 30 km/h) is the only no-fee removable-battery model verified, and is a light-use substitute, not a fair 125cc substitute. Confirmed ZAU's PChome copy says charging at TES public posts is possible and no monthly fee. Plate class and subsidy amount remain unverified, and speed rules for the class must be checked before publishing.
